reasons: Lake identity record verifies the full title, U.S. Supreme Court, docket, date decided, and year 1998.
Lake citations include official cite 524 U.S. 357, parallel cites 118 S. Ct. 2014 and 141 L. Ed. 2d 344, and vendor-neutral cite 1998 U.S. LEXIS 4037.

The stated holding tracks the opinion's express holding that the federal exclusionary rule does not bar introduction at parole revocation hearings of evidence seized in violation of parolees' Fourth Amendment rights.
The lake treatment scope note independently states the same operative proposition.

defect.evidence_quote: We therefore hold that parole boards are not required by federal law to exclude evidence obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment.
defect.problem: The role 'Key — Limiting' on 'The Good-Faith Exception' overclaims the case. The disclosed opinion supports Scott as a limitation on the exclusionary rule in parole-revocation proceedings, not as a key good-faith-exception holding.
defect.proposed_fix: Move the key role to 'The Exclusionary Rule' or downgrade any Good-Faith Exception placement to a related/cross-doctrine deterrence-framework note tied to Leon.

reasons: The case's operative holding is a categorical nonapplication of the federal exclusionary rule at parole revocation hearings.
The opinion discusses Leon and reasonable-reliance examples, but does not decide or limit the good-faith exception itself.
The visible 'Appears on' section identifies 'The Exclusionary Rule' as the key limiting home, which aligns better with the opinion than the frontmatter Good-Faith home.
residual_risks: A Good-Faith page could still mention Scott as related background if that page covers Leon's cost-benefit deterrence framework broadly.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'Related (deterrence framework)' if retained on the Good-Faith Exception page.

reasons: The modest 'Related (cross-doctrine)' role is supported by the opinion's discussion of parole supervision, administrative parole-revocation procedures, and Griffin v. Wisconsin.
The opinion expressly does not decide the constitutionality of the search, so the related-only label avoids overclaiming a special-needs holding.
residual_risks: No home-page text was disclosed, so only the title-level taxonomy and case text could be checked.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the role related-only and avoid implying Scott decided parole-search reasonableness.
